verified.title: Edge thickness barely tapers, so the hierarchy reads poorly
verified.reasoning: Flowmaid strokes are 4.5 (4 trunks) and 3.5 (13 leaves), a 1.29x ratio. Mermaid's CSS has .edge-depth-1{stroke-width:11} on root edges and .edge-depth-3{stroke-width:5} on leaf edges, a 2.2x ratio. In the PNGs, mermaid's trunks are clearly heavier and flowmaid's are barely different.
verified.root_cause: src/mindmap.rs:271: width: (5.5 - n.depth as f64).max(2.0), a 1px step per depth.
verified.fix_sketch: Use a steeper step, e.g. width = (10.0 - 3.0*(depth-1)).max(2.0), giving trunk 10, leaf 7, depth-3 4. Or use a geometric 0.6^depth scale, or a tapered filled polygon (wide at the parent, narrow at the child). Check that thick trunks still hide under small depth-1 chips; their ends are already hidden because edges run centre to centre.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 4.5px trunks, 3.5px leaf edges.
verified.what_mermaid_does: 11px trunks, 5px leaf edges.

verified.title: White text on the orange and green branches has low contrast
verified.reasoning: I recomputed WCAG contrast for white text: #d99114 2.62, #33a35c 3.21, #c2588c 4.14, #5b6dc0 4.78. Labels are 14px regular, so AA needs 4.5. The Engine branch (5 nodes) and the Output branch (4 nodes) fail, 9 of the 17 non-root nodes. Dark #232840 text would give 5.53 on amber and 4.51 on green.
verified.root_cause: src/mindmap.rs:41 BRANCH_TEXT = "#ffffff" is applied to every branch at :239-242, whatever the fill. The fills come from the shared src/style.rs:84-93 ACCENTS palette, which was not picked for white text. There is no luminance or contrast helper anywhere in src/.
verified.fix_sketch: Add a small WCAG relative-luminance helper (style.rs) and choose, per fill, whichever of white and TEXT_COLOR has the higher contrast. That gives dark text on amber and green and white on indigo and rose. Alternatively darken the mindmap fills only (mix about 20% black into the accent) to keep white text everywhere. MindNodeBox.text_color is already per-node, so painters keep working.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: White text on every accent; amber and green fall below 4.5:1.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Black text on light fills (10-20:1); only the purple branch is weak (2.58:1).

verified.title: Text and nodes are undersized relative to the canvas; every node is a uniform 32px chip
verified.reasoning: True: FONT=14 vs mermaid's 16px, and every non-root node is exactly 32px tall. Mermaid's node area is 1.75x flowmaid's, which accounts for about half of the ink gap. Overstated: 'first-level nodes are the least prominent' applies to mermaid too. Its depth-1 default nodes are 34px tall, smaller than its 54-78px rounded leaves. Mermaid's size variety also comes from shape and wrapping, not from hierarchy. 14px is flowmaid's house size across all diagram types. The real gap is that neither renderer sizes nodes by depth, and flowmaid has no thicker trunks to compensate.
verified.root_cause: src/mindmap.rs:22-26 and :35 (PAD_X 12, PAD_Y 7, LINE_H 18, FONT 14). node_size (:87-101) ignores depth. layout::text_width (src/layout.rs:193) assumes 14px.
verified.fix_sketch: Size by depth. Root at 18px bold, depth-1 at 15-16px semibold with PAD_Y 9, leaves at 14px. Scale text_width by font/14, add a font_size field to MindNodeBox (public API), and emit a per-<text> font-size in label_svg.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 14px text; every non-root node 32px tall.
verified.what_mermaid_does: 16px text; heights 34-88 depending on shape and wrapping.

verified.title: Leaf edges bunch into a narrow fan at the parent
verified.reasoning: The geometry checks out. Reach's edges to CLI, Desktop and Web cross its top border (y=257.2) at x≈333.0, 342.9 and 350.1. Input's two edges cross 21px apart. But an outward-facing fan is inherent to any outward radial tree, and it reads acceptably in the PNG. It is a symptom of the same global-ring placement as uneven-long-leaf-spokes, not a separate defect.
verified.root_cause: Same as uneven-long-leaf-spokes: src/mindmap.rs:152-153 places children on a ring centred on the root, so every child lies in the outward half-plane of its parent, in a narrow angular band as seen from the parent.
verified.fix_sketch: The parent-centric fan placement from uneven-long-leaf-spokes spreads the angles automatically (children around 120-150° of the parent's outward side). No separate fix needed.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Three edges leave Reach's top within 17px of each other.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Children surround Reach on several sides.

verified.title: Bang starburst has lopsided spikes and the label nearly touches the notches
verified.reasoning: Lopsided spikes, confirmed: the left/right spikes are 0.26·94 ≈ 24.4px and the top/bottom ones 0.26·23.8 ≈ 6.2px. 'Nearly touches', overstated: I measured the text in Chromium with getBBox at x 115.7-235.6, and the inner valleys at mid-height are at 107.5 and 243.8, so the clearance is about 8px on each side. Tight but not touching.
verified.root_cause: src/mindmap.rs:313-323 star_pts scales the unit star by rx and ry separately (rx*f, ry*f), so spike length is proportional to the semi-axis. On a 188x48 box (sizing at :98, base_w*1.25+6) that gives 4:1 spike lengths. Called at :292 with inner=0.74.
verified.fix_sketch: Offset outer points from the inner ellipse by a constant spike depth (e.g. 8px along the normal) and space them by arc length rather than by angle. Size the inner ellipse so it contains the label box plus 10px: rx_in = (tw/2+10)·√2, ry_in = (h/2+6)·√2.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 16-point star with spikes about 24px long at the sides and about 6px at top and bottom.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Scalloped badge with an even margin.

verified.title: Horizontal padding in the pills is tight; text ends sit inside the rounded caps
verified.reasoning: The padding is 12px against mermaid's 20px. Chromium getBBox shows 11.4-14.2px each side for pills. The 'text inside the rounded caps' part is geometrically misleading. With h=32 and rx=14, the cap boundary at glyph height (±5px from centre) is only about 0.3px inset from the straight edge, so the curvature does not crowd the text. In the zoomed crop, 'Orthogonal routing' looks snug but acceptable. This is a padding preference, not a defect in the curves.
verified.root_cause: src/mindmap.rs:22 PAD_X = 12.0. rx = (h/2).min(14.0) at :393.
verified.fix_sketch: Raise PAD_X to about 16. It feeds node_size, so layout follows automatically.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 12px horizontal padding.
verified.what_mermaid_does: 20px horizontal padding.

verified.title: ::icon(fa fa-file-code) is silently ignored
verified.reasoning: Correct that flowmaid draws nothing, but mermaid's reference SVG has no icon output either (no 'icon' or 'fa-' in its body), so this is not a visible regression. The data is also lost at parse time, so no renderer could ever use it.
verified.root_cause: src/parser.rs:3900: if trimmed.starts_with("::icon(") || trimmed.starts_with(":::") { continue; } discards the decoration. MindNode has no icon field. The same branch silently drops :::class styling.
verified.fix_sketch: Parse the icon class into MindNode.icon: Option<String>. Reserve about 20px for it in node_size and draw a neutral glyph or a small inline-SVG placeholder (no font-awesome). Parse :::class into a style hook the same way.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Parses the line, drops the icon, draws nothing.
verified.what_mermaid_does: In this reference render, also draws no icon.

missed: Cloud and bang size multipliers inflate the layout as well as the shape (moderate). src/mindmap.rs:97 makes the cloud base_w*1.4+8 (227x49, the widest element in the map) where mermaid's is about 164x100, and :98 makes the bang base_w*1.25+6 (188x48). Because angular_half (:107-112) charges each node its full diagonal, the cloud alone takes 2*asin(116/344) ≈ 39° of the depth-2 ring, one of the inputs that forces the 344px ring and the sparse canvas. Evidence: the cloud polygon spans x 30.2-257.5 against a 134.6px label (measured in Chromium), so 46px of padding on each side.

Stale documentation describes a different renderer (minor, not visual). src/render.rs:86-87 says the mindmap is a 'left-to-right tidy tree with colored branches', but it is radial. src/model.rs:1132-1135 says bang is 'approximated as a bold pill' and cloud 'approximated as an ellipse', but they are drawn as a 16-point star and a |sin| polygon. Anyone tuning the shapes from these docs will be misled.

Tightening the rings alone creates the opposite problem, which matters for any fix plan. In my scratch prototype (RING=120 plus tangent-projected footprints; build in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/fm, render at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/exp1.png), the canvas shrank to 715x564, but Reach->Eleven diagram types fell to a 19px visible edge and Engine->Orthogonal routing to 26px, while Reach->Web stayed at 127px. Uneven spoke length is built into the global-ring model; shrinking the canvas and evening the spokes need separate fixes.

name: journey
diagram_type: journey
overall_verdict: For this journey, flowmaid looks cleaner and easier to read than mermaid 12. Its canvas is compact (573x250 against 1300x540), faces are large and color-coded by score, labels sit right under each face, and the legend is centered. Mermaid's default is sparse and dated: a big empty gutter, tiny cream faces, a long axis arrow, and dashed lines that run into empty space. Flowmaid's real weaknesses are in what the picture means, not in polish. Every face sits on one flat line, so the satisfaction curve that a journey map exists to show is gone. The same blue and green are reused for sections, actors and scores. The two section bars touch, leaving notches where their rounded corners meet. Fix those three and flowmaid clearly beats the reference.
flowmaid_better: Compact, balanced canvas: 573x250 against mermaid's viewBox of 0 -25 1300 540. Mermaid wastes about 95px on a left legend gutter, leaves 300px or more empty to the right of the axis arrow (the arrow ends near x=1735 in the PNG, the canvas is 1960 wide), and runs dashed task lines down to y=450, well below the lowest face.

Score is shown two ways: face fill on a 5-step red-to-green scale (#e8574f, #f0894e, #f2c94c, #9fcf6a, #57b563) and a mouth curve that scales with the score (curv = (score-3)*r*0.28). Mermaid's faces are all cream #FFF8DC with a #999 stroke, r=15, and have only 3 expressions, so 4 and 5 look the same.
Faces are r=22 with clear eyes and mouth. Mermaid's r=15 faces with 1.5px eyes are hard to read at normal size.
Each task label sits directly under its face. In mermaid you have to follow a dashed line from the task box (y=110-160) down to a face 140-260px lower.

Actor dots never collide. In mermaid the r=7 actor circles straddle the top border of each task box (cy=110 on a box edge at y=110), and on 'Do work' the two circles overlap (cx=564 and cx=574, r=7, so they overlap by 4px).

Actor colors are easy to tell apart (blue #5b6dc0, green #33a35c) and the legend follows source order (Me, Cat). Mermaid uses lawn green #7CFC00 against dark sea green #8FBC8F with black strokes, lists Cat before Me, and puts the legend in a cramped left gutter at x=20.
Title, legend and content share one centered axis. Mermaid's left-aligned 4ex title is cut off from the legend, which sits at the far left.
No stray axis arrow or dashed lines that end at nothing.

verified.title: Every face sits on one baseline, so there is no satisfaction curve and the connecting polyline is always flat
verified.reasoning: Confirmed in the flowmaid SVG: all five face circles have cy=170.0 and the polyline is '76,170 ... 496.7,170' even though the scores are 5,3,1,5,5. Mermaid's renderer sets the face position with `cy: 300 + (5 - task.score) * 30` (journeyDiagram chunk, line 940), and its SVG has faces at 300/360/420/300/300. The polyline is the worst part: it draws a curve that carries no information and suggests a steady journey. Color plus mouth still show the score, but scores 4 and 5 are hard to tell apart (#9fcf6a vs #57b563, Bezier control offsets 6.2 vs 12.3).
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:155 `let face_cy = y + DOTS_H + FACE_R;` is computed once per diagram and never depends on t.score. src/journey.rs:186 `path.push((cx, face_cy))` and :200 `cy: face_cy` give every task that same value. label_y (:156) and height (:157) also assume a single face row.
verified.fix_sketch: Add `const SCORE_STEP: f64 = 12.0;`. For each task set `cy = face_cy_top + (5 - score) as f64 * SCORE_STEP`, where face_cy_top = y + DOTS_H + FACE_R. Use it for both the TaskGlyph and the path point. Put every label on one shared baseline under the lowest possible face (`label_y = face_cy_top + 4*SCORE_STEP + FACE_R + 14`) and grow height by 4*SCORE_STEP, about 48px. Leave the actor dots on the common top row. The existing tests (inside-canvas checks) still pass, and there are no journey snapshot fixtures.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Face y = 300 + (5-score)*30, so the faces trace the emotional curve.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Uses a constant face_cy for all tasks. The 'journey path' polyline is a horizontal line.

verified.title: The same accent colors encode section, actor and (nearly) score
verified.reasoning: Confirmed. Section 0 and actor 0 are both #5b6dc0, and section 1 and actor 1 are both #33a35c. The legend (circle bottom y=79) sits 9px above the bars (y=88), in the same order and the same colors, which invites reading 'Go to work = Me, Go home = Cat'. The score-5 face #57b563 is the same hue family as the actor/section green #33a35c, so green carries three meanings. Mermaid keeps these apart: pastel section fills #ECECFF/#ffffde, actor fills #8FBC8F/#7CFC00, and neutral faces #FFF8DC. The 'heavier than the title' remark is subjective, but the collision itself is objective.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:176 `color: accent(si)` for section bands, :196 `accent(a)` for per-task dots and :221 `accent(a)` for legend items all index the same ACCENTS table (src/style.rs:83-92, where index 1 is green #33a35c). The score scale is in src/journey.rs:46-54 (5 => #57b563).
verified.fix_sketch: Give sections their own palette: light tints of the accents (e.g. #e4e7f6, #ddf1e4, #f8ecd4 …) with TEXT_COLOR labels and an optional 1px accent stroke. That keeps sections recessive, matches mermaid's pastel look and also fixes the contrast issue. For actors, use an order that skips green/red/amber so they never look like score colors (e.g. indigo, rose, violet, teal, steel blue), or draw actor dots with a ring/outline style.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Pastel section/task fills, distinct actor colors, neutral face color. No color has two meanings.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: accent(i) is used for both section i and actor i, and the green score-5 face nearly matches the accent green.

verified.title: Section bands touch edge to edge, and their rx=6 corners cut notches at the join
verified.reasoning: Confirmed. 'Go to work' spans x=24..336 and 'Go home' spans x=336..548.7, both with rx=6. scratchpad/cmp/zj/junction.png shows the V notches at the top and bottom of the join, and they are faintly visible at native scale in the PNG at x≈516. One correction to the first pass's evidence: mermaid's 'Go home' box is x=750..1100 (width 350), not 750..1050. Mermaid's 50px gap is also just its uniform inter-task gap (task boxes 150 wide on a 200 pitch), not deliberate section spacing. I lowered severity to 1 because this is cosmetic and nothing is lost.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:116-122 accumulates `x += w` across all tasks with no extra gap at section boundaries. src/journey.rs:168-169 sets each band's x0/x1 to exactly the outer column edges, so neighboring bands share the edge x. src/journey.rs:252 rounds all four corners (rx=6).
verified.fix_sketch: Add `const SECTION_GAP: f64 = 8.0;` and in the column loop add it to x when a task starts a new section (track section boundaries while flattening). Bands then get a visible gutter, and the face row gets a matching extra gap at the boundary. A minimal alternative is to inset each band by 2px on each side (x0+2, w-4).
verified.what_mermaid_does: Leaves 50px between all task/section boxes ('Go to work' 150..700, 'Go home' 750..1100).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Bands abut at x=336, and the rounded corners leave notches.

verified.title: White bold 13px section label on green (and amber/teal) accent fails WCAG AA
verified.reasoning: I recomputed the ratios. White on #33a35c is 3.21:1 and white on #5b6dc0 is 4.78:1, which matches the claim. The first pass missed that it gets worse with three or more sections: accent 2 (#d99114 amber) is 2.62:1, teal #199a8e is 3.47, coral #d96459 is 3.55, steel #4d8fbf is 3.50 and rose #c2588c is 4.14. So most of the palette fails for 13px bold text.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:259 hardcodes `fill="#ffffff"` for section labels, regardless of the band color from accent(si) (src/style.rs:83-92).
verified.fix_sketch: Either switch to pastel section fills with TEXT_COLOR (see palette-collision), or pick the label color by contrast: compute the band's relative luminance and use #232840 whenever white falls below 4.5:1. A small helper in style.rs would do it.
verified.what_mermaid_does: #333 text on pastel fills, high contrast.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: White bold text on saturated accents: 3.21:1 on green and 2.62:1 on amber.

verified.title: Actor legend is shifted about 9px left of the canvas center
verified.reasoning: Confirmed numerically. The Me item starts at x=231.9, and 'Cat' ends at 301.4 + ~21.4 = 322.8, so the visible center is ≈277.4 while the canvas/title center is 286.35. In the PNG the offset is about 13px at 1.54x scale, which matches. The cause is that the trailing 18px gap is included in the centering width.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:132 `item_w = 16 + text_width(name) + 18` includes the inter-item gap. :133 sums it over all items, so the last item's trailing 18px is counted too. :215 centers with `(width - legend_total) / 2`. The canvas width check at :135-136 also overcounts by 18px.
verified.fix_sketch: Use `let legend_vis = legend_total - 18.0` (when there are actors) for both the centering at :215 and legend_w at :136. Keep item_w for advancing lx.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Fixed left-column legend, so centering does not apply.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The centered row includes a phantom 18px trailing gap and lands about 9px left of center.

verified.title: Sad mouth is shallow and sits high, with its apex at eye level between the eyes
verified.reasoning: The geometry is right, but the comparison with mermaid is wrong. Mermaid's sad mouth is the upper half of a circle of radius 7.5, whose chord is at translate(625,427). The arc rises to y=419.5, so its apex is 0.03r above the face center at 420. That is the same relative height as flowmaid's apex (169.15, i.e. cy-0.04r). So mermaid does not put the frown's peak lower. What differs is the shape: mermaid's frown is deep (0.5r tall, chord at +0.47r), while flowmaid's is shallow (0.28r tall, chord at +0.24r). In flowmaid the mouth stroke top (≈168.35) is only about 0.15px below the eye bottoms (168.2), but that point is horizontally between the eyes. Directly under each eye the mouth is at y≈172.7, about 4.5px clear, so nothing overlaps. The zoomed face (zj/face.png) still reads as sad. It is somewhat cramped, and the lower ~40% of the disc is empty. The 'worried/wincing' reading is subjective.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:352 `let my = cy + r * 0.24;` fixes the mouth chord for every score. :353 `curv = (score-3)*r*0.28` moves only the control point, so for frowns the curve rises from a high chord toward the eye line.
verified.fix_sketch: Move the chord down for negative curvature, e.g. `let my = cy + r*0.24 + (-curv).max(0.0)*0.6;`. For score 1 that puts the chord at about cy+0.58r and the apex at about cy+0.3r. Optionally deepen the frown slightly. Smiles stay as they are.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Semicircular frown, chord at cy+0.47r, apex at cy-0.03r (deep arc).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Shallow quadratic frown, chord at cy+0.24r, apex at cy-0.04r, crowding the eye line.

verified.title: Per-task actor dots (r=4) are smaller than legend dots (r=6) and tiny next to r=22 faces
verified.reasoning: Confirmed. Task dots are r=4.0 and legend dots are r=6. The dot bottom is at y=144 and the face stroke top at ≈147.3, about 3.3px apart. The size mismatch is real, though the readability impact is modest. Mermaid uses r=7 for both.
verified.root_cause: src/journey.rs:29 `DOT_R: f64 = 4.0` for task dots, while the legend radius is hardcoded at src/journey.rs:315 (`r="6"`, with the matching +6.0 offset at :316). DOTS_H=16 (:31) leaves little clearance above the face.
verified.fix_sketch: Use one constant for both (e.g. 5.0), have the legend circle use it, and raise DOTS_H to about 20 so there are 5px or more between dot and face.
verified.what_mermaid_does: r=7 for both legend and task actor circles.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Legend r=6 and task dots r=4, with about 3px between dot and face.

verified.title: Actor dots lack <title> tooltips; accessible name ignores accTitle (the title-vs-mermaid part is overstated)
verified.reasoning: Tooltips: confirmed. Mermaid writes <title>Me</title> and <title>Cat</title> inside each actor circle, and flowmaid's dots are bare self-closing circles. Generic title: overstated as a mermaid gap. Mermaid's root SVG here has no <title> and no aria-label at all (only aria-roledescription="journey"), because mermaid fills the accessible name only from accTitle, never from `title`. The real defect is the one the first pass did not test. I rendered a journey containing `accTitle: Accessible journey name` and `accDescr: ...`, and flowmaid still emitted aria-label="User journey" with no <desc>. The parser discards the acc statements for journeys, while class/er/seq honor them.
verified.root_cause: Tooltips: src/journey.rs:283-288 emits `<circle .../>` with no child. TaskGlyph.actor_dots (:78) carries only (x, y, color), with no actor name. Title: src/journey.rs:247 calls `svg_open(..., "User journey", opts)` rather than svg_open_a11y. src/parser.rs:4028 `let (source, _acc) = extract_acc(...)` throws the accTitle/accDescr away (its comment says this is because of struct-literal API compatibility).
verified.fix_sketch: (1) Add the actor name to actor_dots and write `<circle ...><title>{name}</title></circle>`. Optionally give each face a `<title>{task}: {score}</title>`. (2) Store the A11y on Journey (a new field, or a side channel through Document/render to avoid the public struct-literal break) and call `svg_open_a11y(&mut s, ..., &title, desc, opts)` with `A11y::resolve(d.title or "User journey")`, so accTitle wins, then `title`, then the default.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Writes <title>Me</title> per actor circle. Uses accTitle/accDescr for the root accessible name and description, and ignores `title` for it.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: No dot tooltips. Always writes aria-label/<title> 'User journey', even when accTitle/accDescr are given.

missed: SEVERITY 2 - A long section name overflows its band and is lost. Section band width is just the sum of its task columns, which are sized from task names only. The bold white section label is drawn unclipped, so the part outside the band is white on the white canvas (invisible), and the next band, painted afterwards, covers the right-hand overflow. Repro: scratchpad/jr/a.mmd ('section Commute to the office early in the morning' with one task 'Tea') renders only 'the office early in', cut off by the 104px band and the green band (scratchpad/jr/a.png). Root cause: src/journey.rs:117-122 (column width = max(text_width(task)+20, COL_MIN), section name ignored) and src/journey.rs:256-263 (no fit, wrap or ellipsis). Fix (S): after building cols, for each section compute need = bold_width(name)+24 (text_width*~1.1). If the sum of its column widths is smaller, spread the deficit across that section's columns before computing centres. Mermaid wraps the section label inside a foreignObject.

SEVERITY 1-2 - Scores that mermaid accepts make the whole diagram fail to parse. flowmaid parses the score as u8 (src/parser.rs:4081-4084), so `X: 3.5: Me` gives 'parse error — line N: invalid journey score: 3.5' and `C: -1: Me` fails the same way. Mermaid uses `score = Number(pieces[0])` (journeyDiagram chunk ~line 644) and renders both. Fix (S): parse as f64 and clamp to 1..=5, then round for color and mouth (or store f64 and interpolate cy for the score-height fix).

SEVERITY 1 - Many actors on one task overflow the column and the canvas padding. Actor dots go in a single unwrapped row and column width ignores the dot row. Repro: one task with 12 actors places dots from x=6 to x=146 inside a column spanning 24..128, so they cross the 24px canvas margin on the left and spill into the next task's column on the right (scratchpad/jr/b.svg). Root cause: src/journey.rs:188-198 (single row) and :118 (column width ignores n*(2*DOT_R)+(n-1)*DOT_GAP). Fix (S): include the dot-row width in the column width, or wrap dots onto a second row and grow DOTS_H.

SEVERITY 1 - Actor colors repeat after 8. ACCENTS has 8 entries (src/style.rs:83-92), so the 9th actor gets #5b6dc0, the same as the 1st, and the two are indistinguishable in the legend and on the task dots (scratchpad/jr/a.png: 'Me' and 'Elk'). Mermaid also wraps, after 6 colors (conf.actorColours), so this matches mermaid, but flowmaid offers no secondary cue such as an outline or pattern.

SEVERITY 1 - Contrast gets worse with more sections: the third section band (amber #d99114) gives white-on-amber at 2.62:1, and teal, coral and steel blue are about 3.5:1 (same root cause as section-label-contrast, src/journey.rs:259).

SEVERITY 1 - Long task names never wrap. A column grows to the full label width (src/journey.rs:118), so one long task name makes a very wide canvas and uneven face spacing. In scratchpad/jr/a.png one label is about 500px wide and the faces are 278px apart. Mermaid wraps task text inside fixed 150px boxes. Fix (M): cap the column width (e.g. 160px) and wrap labels onto multiple lines, as timeline.rs already does with svg_text_multiline, growing LABEL_H to fit.

name: gitgraph
diagram_type: gitGraph
overall_verdict: Flowmaid gets the topology right: it uses the same lanes and commit order as mermaid and draws every commit, branch, merge and tag. It looks weak for three reasons. All connectors are thin navy 2px threads with no branch color, so the colored "subway map" look is lost. The cross-lane edges are lopsided curves that leave a commit flat and arrive on a steep diagonal, and one of them cuts through the "merge-hotfix" label mid-word. Merge, REVERSE, HIGHLIGHT and tags are barely marked or look the same, so meaning mermaid makes obvious is lost. Its horizontal 13px labels and calmer palette read better than mermaid's 10px rotated labels on smudgy backgrounds, but overall it looks like a draft next to mermaid.

Mermaid's are 10px, rotated -45deg, on semi-transparent #ffffde (opacity .5) rects that look like smudges.
