Calmer palette (#5b6dc0 / #33a35c / #d99114). Mermaid's default is saturated pure blue hsl(240,100%,46%), acid yellow #DEDE00 and lime #9DEC00, which look garish.
The commit sequence and lane assignment match mermaid exactly: init, a, b, c, merge-feat, fix, merge-hotfix, release in the same columns and on the same lanes.
Self-contained SVG: 3.7 KB, explicit attributes, no id-scoped CSS, with <title> and aria-label. Mermaid's is 13 KB and relies on a class-based stylesheet.
Larger 24px commit dots and readable label sizes. The tags do not overlap any geometry.

verified.title: Every connector is the same navy color, so the lines carry no branch identity
verified.reasoning: All 9 <path> elements in gitgraph.flowmaid.svg have stroke="#44507a" stroke-width="2". Mermaid's paths carry arrow0/1/2 classes: the fork and merge are colored by the lower-lane branch (yellow for feat, lime for hotfix), and the trunk uses arrow0. Four identical navy lines do meet at merge-feat (460,30). This is the biggest visual gap between the two renders. Interaction to watch: once forks are colored, the init->a fork, which is painted after the main edges, will visibly paint over the trunk for about 30px (see fork-overlaps-trunk). Fix the edge geometry in the same change.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:332-339. to_svg_with formats each edge with the constant EDGE_COLOR (scene.rs:50, #44507a). SceneEdge carries no color, and scene() (gitgraph.rs:157-208) records no branch for an edge even though it knows it: the fork's child branch, b.order for the window edges, and the merge source's branch.
verified.fix_sketch: In scene() record one color per edge, either as a new GitScene field `edge_colors: Vec<&'static str>` parallel to scene.edges or by putting a GitEdge wrapper next to each SceneEdge. Fork (l.161) gets accent(d.commits[first].branch), same-branch windows (l.179) get accent(b.order), merges (l.198) get accent(d.commits[sp].branch). This matches mermaid's rule that a cross-lane edge takes the lower lane's color. In to_svg_with, use that color instead of EDGE_COLOR. A version with no API change is also possible: in to_svg_with, color an edge by the endpoint with the larger lane order, looking it up by e.from/e.to, and use the node stroke because a REVERSE node's fill is white.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Colors each connector by branch class (.arrowN): the feat fork and merge in yellow, the hotfix fork and merge in lime, the trunk in blue.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Every edge is #44507a. Branch color shows only on the dots and the lane-name text.

verified.title: Merge curves run through the commit labels under the merge commits
verified.reasoning: Sampling the cubic M550 170 C595 170 595 170 640 30 gives x=630.0 at y=61.0 and x=632.4 at y=53.7. With Helvetica metrics the label 'merge-hotfix' spans about 604-676, and its glyph band is y≈50-62. A 4x crop of the PNG shows the stroke going right through the 'ge' of merge-hotfix. The b->merge-feat curve is at (427,55.5) and (431,52.3), and the crop shows it clipping the top-left of the 'm' in 'merge-feat' (that label spans about 428.6-491.4). Labels are drawn after edges but have no background or halo, so the line shows through the letters.
verified.root_cause: Two causes together. (1) src/gitgraph.rs:121-130 puts every commit id centered directly under its commit (x, y+R+14), and write_label (gitgraph.rs:365-380) emits bare <text> with no knock-out halo or background. (2) edge_bezier (gitgraph.rs:297-301) puts both control points at (cx, p0.y), so a merge from a lower lane reaches the merge commit along a straight chord from (cx, p0.y). The last ~30px of that chord cut through the label band beneath the target.
verified.fix_sketch: Quick mitigation (S): give commit-id text a halo, `paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="4" stroke-linejoin="round"`. Proper fix (M), done together with the elbow routing in hockey-stick-curves: any commit that owns a downward vertical leg (a fork parent with children on lower lanes, or a merge target fed from below) has that leg pass straight down through a centered label. For those commits, either move the id to anchor=start at x+R/2+3, or rotate it -45 degrees as mermaid does by default (rotateCommitLabel). Combine this with label-aware column pitch so the moved label cannot run into the next column's label.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Merge legs climb vertically at the merge commit's x. Labels are rotated -45 degrees and offset down-left on semi-opaque backgrounds, so no word is struck through.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Steep chord-shaped merge curves arrive through the centered label below the merge commit: merge-hotfix is struck through and merge-feat is grazed.

verified.title: Cross-lane edges are lopsided curves that leave flat and arrive on a steep diagonal
verified.reasoning: The paths match the claim exactly. With c1==c2==(cx,p0.y), the curve leaves tangent to the source lane and arrives along the chord from (cx,p0.y) to p1. The arrival angle is atan(|dy|/(|dx|/2)): 57 degrees for init->a, 38 for b->merge-feat, 72 for merge-feat->fix and for fix->merge-hotfix. Each edge therefore arrives at a different angle, and the hotfix excursion renders as a lopsided V. Mermaid instead uses 'L 10 68 A 20 20 0 0 0 30 88 L 60 88'-style elbows.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:297-301. In edge_bezier the LR branch returns [(p0),(cx,p0.y),(cx,p0.y),(p1)], and the TB/BT branch (302-305) uses the mirrored form with (p0.x,cy) twice. This degenerate cubic never becomes tangent to the target lane. to_svg_with (332-339) only knows how to write one cubic per edge.
verified.fix_sketch: Smallest fix (S): put the control point at the elbow corner, so the vertical leg is at the upper-lane endpoint and the horizontal run is on the lower lane. For a fork (p1 lower) c1=c2=(p0.x,p1.y). For a merge (p0 lower) c1=c2=(p1.x,p0.y). The curve then leaves and arrives with consistent tangents. Mermaid-like fix (M): add an elbow_path(p0,p1,orient) helper that emits 'M x0 y0 L x0 y1∓r A r r 0 0 s x0±r y1 L x1 y1' (or H-then-V for merges) with r=min(20,|dx|/2,|dy|/2). Use it in to_svg_with. Also fill SceneEdge.waypoints with the corner polyline so generic Scene painters get a similar shape. Add a TB/BT mirror of the helper. Re-place labels at the same time (see label-strikethrough), because the vertical legs land on label centers.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Orthogonal routing with 20px rounded elbows: a vertical leg at the upper-lane commit and a horizontal run on the lower lane.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Degenerate cubics that hug the source lane, then arrive on a straight diagonal at 38-72 degrees.

verified.title: Fork curves run along the main line before peeling off
verified.reasoning: The geometry is real. For the init->a cubic, y(t)=30+70*t^3, so the curve stays within 2px of the trunk until t≈0.31, which is x≈131. That is about 19px beyond the circle rim at x=112. The merge-feat->fix edge does the same until x≈491. A 5x zoom shows the trunk visibly thickened for roughly 15-20px right of each commit before the fork separates. However, the fork still reads as a fillet coming out of the commit, not as a branch starting partway between init and c, so the perception claim is overstated. This becomes more visible once edges are branch-colored, because the colored fork is drawn on top of the trunk.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:297-301, the same degenerate edge_bezier as hockey-stick-curves. Both control points sit on the source lane (y=p0.y), so the vertical deviation grows as dy*t^3 and stays on the trunk for the first ~30% of the curve.
verified.fix_sketch: Fixed by the elbow change in hockey-stick-curves: forks leave vertically from the parent (c1=c2=(p0.x,p1.y), or the explicit V-arc-H path), so no part of the fork lies on the trunk.
verified.what_mermaid_does: The fork drops straight down from the parent commit (M 10 -2 L 10 68 ...).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The fork starts horizontally on top of the trunk and only separates about 20px past the circle rim.

verified.title: Hairline 2px edges under large dots
verified.reasoning: The facts are right. Every edge is stroke-width="2" under r=12 circles with a 2px stroke, against mermaid's stroke-width 8 with round caps under r=10 circles, and the flowmaid render does look like beads on a thread. The claim that the trunk has no weight relative to the side branches is not a difference, because mermaid draws every branch line at the same 8px too. That part is not a defect relative to mermaid.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:336, where to_svg_with hard-codes `stroke-width="2"` and sets no linecap. R=12.0 at gitgraph.rs:27.
verified.fix_sketch: Add an EDGE_W const of about 4-5 and emit `stroke-linecap="round"`. Optionally drop R to 10 so the line-to-dot ratio is closer to mermaid's 8:20. This also makes the branch colors from monochrome-edges readable.
verified.what_mermaid_does: 8px round-capped branch lines under r=10 commits.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 2px lines under r=12 dots, which look wispy.

verified.title: Merge commits look exactly like normal commits
verified.reasoning: The circles at cx=460 and cx=640 are byte-identical in style to init at cx=100: fill and stroke #5b6dc0, r=12. Mermaid adds an r=6 #ECECFF circle with class commit-merge at both merge commits, and the left render shows them as rings with light centers.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:267-283. commit_color matches only on c.kind, and the parser always sets merges to CommitKind::Normal (parser.rs:4419). to_svg_with (342-351) emits exactly one <circle> per SceneNode, and SceneNode carries no merge flag even though c.second_parent.is_some() is known in scene().
verified.fix_sketch: Record per-commit glyph info, for example a GitScene `glyphs: Vec<Glyph{merge,kind}>` parallel to scene.nodes. In to_svg_with, when merge is true, add `<circle r="R*0.5" fill="#fff"/>` (or #eef0fa) over the colored disc.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Merge commits get an inner r=6 light circle over the branch-colored r=10 circle.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Merge commits are plain filled discs, identical to normal commits.

verified.title: A REVERSE commit is drawn as a hollow ring, which reads as a merge or empty commit, not a revert
verified.reasoning: 'release' renders as <circle fill="#ffffff" stroke="#5b6dc0">, a white ring with no cross. Mermaid draws the filled branch-colored circle with a light X (path M 355,-7L365,3M355,3L365,-7, class commit-reverse, stroke-width 3). Mermaid's own merge glyph is a colored ring with a light center, so flowmaid's REVERSE looks like mermaid's merge marker and the meaning is effectively inverted.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:274-277, where commit_color maps CommitKind::Reverse to fill "#ffffff". to_svg_with (342-351) can only emit a circle, so there is no way to draw a cross.
verified.fix_sketch: Keep the fill as branch_color for Reverse. In to_svg_with, after the circle, emit `<path d="M x-5 y-5 L x+5 y+5 M x-5 y+5 L x+5 y-5" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round"/>` (scaled to R*0.42). This needs the per-node kind from the glyph vector in no-merge-glyph.
verified.what_mermaid_does: A filled branch-colored disc with a light X across it.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: A white-filled ring with no X.

verified.title: A HIGHLIGHT commit differs only by a thin 2px dark ring
verified.reasoning: 'fix' is <circle r="12.0" fill="#d99114" stroke="#232840" stroke-width="2.0">. In the PNG the dark ring is visible on close inspection, but it is the only difference from a normal commit. Mermaid draws a 20x20 dark-violet square with a 12x12 light inner square, which cannot be missed among the circles.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:278-281. CommitKind::Highlight only swaps the stroke to TEXT_COLOR, and to_svg_with (342-351) always emits a circle.
verified.fix_sketch: In to_svg_with, for Highlight emit `<rect x-R y-R 2R 2R fill=darker(branch)>` plus an inner `<rect>` of about 1.2R in white or branch color, or at least a thick 4px dark ring plus an outer halo. This uses the same per-node kind info as reverse-as-hollow.
verified.what_mermaid_does: An outer square in a highlight color with a light inner square.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The same circle with a 2px #232840 outline.

verified.title: Tags are bare bold text styled exactly like the branch label 'main'
verified.reasoning: <text ... font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#5b6dc0">v1.0</text> and the 'main' label use the same size, weight and color. Mermaid uses a luggage-tag polygon with a hole and 10px text. In the flowmaid render, 'v1.0' and 'v1.1' read like column headings.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:132-143. The tag GitLabel uses font_size FONT, font_weight Some("bold") and color color.stroke, the same as the branch labels at gitgraph.rs:214-223. write_label draws only text with no container.
verified.fix_sketch: Draw each tag as a small pill or luggage polygon: width = crate::layout::text_width(tag)*11/13 + 12, light fill (#eef0fa), 1px branch-colored border, 11px normal-weight dark text, and optionally a 1.5px hole circle. Reserve vertical room for it (see tag-top-margin).
verified.what_mermaid_does: A luggage-tag polygon (#ECECFF) with a hole and 10px text.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Bold 13px branch-colored text, identical to the lane-name style.

verified.title: No lane lines: branch names float far from their commits
verified.reasoning: The flowmaid SVG has no lane <line> or <path>. 'hotfix' sits at x=30 while its only commit is at x=550. Mermaid draws a dashed 1px .branch line for each lane across the full width (x 0 to 400) and puts each name in a colored rx=4 pill.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:326-339. to_svg_with writes the branch labels and then the edges, with no lane primitive. scene() (211-245) records the lane positions only implicitly through the branch_labels' y (or x in TB/BT).
verified.fix_sketch: Before the edges, emit for each branch label `<line x1=PAD+BRANCH_LABEL_W-10 y1=l.y x2=width-PAD y2=l.y stroke="#c8ccd8" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="2 3"/>`, with x and y swapped for TB/BT. Optionally put the branch name in an accent-filled pill with white or dark text, which also fixes the low contrast.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Full-width dashed lane guides and pill-shaped branch labels.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: No lane guides. The branch names are loose text in the left column.

verified.title: Merge edges are marked as arrows in the scene, but the SVG writer never draws arrowheads
verified.reasoning: The code fact is true. scene() sets EdgeKind::Arrow on merges, with the comment 'Use an arrowhead so the merge direction reads clearly', and to_svg_with ignores e.kind. The SVG has no <marker>. The visible result, no arrowheads, actually matches mermaid. So this is not a render defect against mermaid. It is an internal inconsistency: the comment is misleading, and any consumer of the public GitScene.scene would draw arrowheads that the SVG does not. Nothing in the crate besides to_svg currently consumes it (render.rs:111/116).
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:192-203, where the merge loop sets `kind: EdgeKind::Arrow`. to_svg_with (332-339) never reads e.kind.
verified.fix_sketch: Set the kind to EdgeKind::Open and rewrite the comment so it agrees with mermaid and the SVG. Alternatively keep Arrow and emit a small marker-end in to_svg_with. The first option is preferred.
verified.what_mermaid_does: No arrowheads. Direction is shown through color and routing.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The scene says Arrow and the SVG draws none, so the two disagree.

verified.title: The amber and green lane names have low contrast on white
verified.reasoning: WCAG contrast on white: #d99114 is 2.62:1, #33a35c is 3.21:1, #5b6dc0 is 4.78:1. Bold 13px is not large text (that needs at least 18.67px bold), so the 4.5:1 threshold applies, and hotfix and feat fail it. The tag text uses the same branch color and has the same problem.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:222/232/242 set `color: accent(b.order)` on the lane-name text, and tags use color.stroke at gitgraph.rs:141. The palette is style.rs:84-93.
verified.fix_sketch: Put lane names in accent-filled pills with the text color chosen by luminance (white or #232840), as mermaid does, or darken the text by about 35% while keeping the dot colors.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Names in filled pills with high-contrast text.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Accent-colored bold text on white, at 2.6:1 and 3.2:1.

verified.title: Tags sit about 2-3px from the top edge of the viewBox
verified.reasoning: I rasterized the flowmaid SVG at 8x with no harness padding. The first dark pixel of 'v1.0' is at svg y≈2.4. The tag sits at y = 30 - 12 - 10 = 8 with dominant-baseline middle, and the canvas top margin does not count tags. Mermaid's viewBox starts at -36.7 with the tag top at -28.7, about 8px of clearance.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:67 and 76. branch_axis_len and branch_pos start lane 0 at PAD, whether or not tags exist. The tag y is y - R - 10.0 at gitgraph.rs:135.
verified.fix_sketch: Compute `top = PAD + if d.commits.iter().any(|c| c.tag.is_some() && c.branch==0) {18.0} else {0.0}`. Use it in branch_pos and in branch_axis_len for LR. Apply the analogous left inset in TB/BT, which is currently much worse (see missed).
verified.what_mermaid_does: About 8px of clearance above the tags.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Tag glyph tops about 2.4px below y=0.

verified.title: Fixed 90px column pitch makes the graph wide and sparse
verified.reasoning: The facts are right: COMMIT_DX=90 and BRANCH_DY=70 give a 772x212 viewBox (3.6:1), against mermaid's 50px commit pitch and 507x254 viewBox. But with horizontal labels, 90px is close to the minimum for this diagram: 'merge-hotfix' is about 72px wide and 'release' about 46px, a gap of about 29px. A blanket 50px pitch would make the labels collide. The real defect is that the pitch ignores label widths in both directions: it is wasteful for 'a', 'b' and 'c' and too small for long ids (see missed). 'Stretched' is a mild matter of taste.
verified.root_cause: src/gitgraph.rs:23 (COMMIT_DX = 90.0) and 77 (commit_pos = PAD + BRANCH_LABEL_W + seq*COMMIT_DX), with no label measurement.
verified.fix_sketch: Replace commit_pos with a cumulative x[]: x[i] = x[i-1] + max(MIN_DX≈50, (w_i + w_j)/2 + 10), where j is the previous commit whose label shares a row with commit i (same lane in LR) and w comes from crate::layout::text_width. Derive the canvas width from max(x + w/2) (see missed).
verified.what_mermaid_does: 50px commit pitch with rotated labels, 507x254.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: A fixed 90px pitch whatever the label width, 772x212.

missed: Long commit ids collide (latent, severity 3; the first pass praised horizontal labels without testing them). Ids are horizontal and centered, the pitch is a fixed 90px, and nothing is measured, so any two consecutive same-lane ids longer than about 13 characters overlap. Repro: commit ids 'initial-scaffold' and 'add-authentication' render as one run-together string, 'initial-scaffoldadd-authentication' (checked visually at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/t/long.png). Mermaid avoids this by rotating ids -45 degrees. Cause: src/gitgraph.rs:23 (COMMIT_DX) and 121-130 (id at x, y+R+14, anchor middle, width never measured).

The canvas size ignores label extents, so text is clipped or runs into the graph. commit_axis_len (src/gitgraph.rs:66) is PAD+BRANCH_LABEL_W+max_seq*COMMIT_DX+R+PAD and counts only the circle radius. A long last id is cut off at the right edge: 'release-candidate-final' renders as 'release-candidate-' in a 412px viewBox, as long.png shows. BRANCH_LABEL_W is a fixed 70px (gitgraph.rs:21), so 'feature/login-page' (bold, about 120px) runs from x=30 to about 150, past the first commit column at x=100. It would overlap any commit or fork on that lane in columns 0-1.

In TB/BT orientation, tags on the main lane are pushed off-canvas. Tags are placed at x-R-4 with anchor end (src/gitgraph.rs:116-119), and lane 0 sits at x=PAD=30, so the tag ends at x=14 and extends to negative x. Repro: `gitGraph TB` / `commit id: "init" tag: "v0.1-alpha"` gives <text x="14.0" text-anchor="end">v0.1-alpha</text> in a viewBox starting at 0, so the tag is almost entirely clipped.

Mermaid's documented orientation syntax with a colon is rejected. `gitGraph TB:` (also LR: and BT:) fails with "parse error — line 1: unknown gitGraph orientation: 'TB:'". I confirmed that mermaid 12.2.0 renders both `gitGraph TB:` and `gitGraph LR:`. Cause: src/parser.rs:43-55, where parse_git_orientation matches the bare rest of the line without trimming a trailing ':'. Fix: rest.trim_end_matches(':').trim() (S).

Parser gaps that quietly change the output (latent, not hit by this diagram). `branch dev order: 2` creates a branch literally named 'dev order: 2', because src/parser.rs:4329-4331 takes the whole rest of the line as the name. `merge dev type: HIGHLIGHT` is accepted but the type is dropped, because merge commits are hard-coded to CommitKind::Normal at src/parser.rs:4419. Both are supported by mermaid.

Fixes interact and need to land together. Coloring edges alone (monochrome-edges) makes the fork-on-trunk overlap visible as a colored stripe painted over the trunk. Switching to mermaid-style elbows alone puts vertical legs straight through the centered ids under merge and fork commits (merge-feat, merge-hotfix, init), which is worse than today's strike-through. Label placement, label-aware pitch, edge geometry and edge color must change in one pass.

name: timeline
diagram_type: timeline
overall_verdict: For this input flowmaid gives the more correct and more compact picture. mermaid 12.2.0 silently drops the three periods declared before the first `section` (2002, 2004, 2005) and spreads three columns over a 995x643 canvas. flowmaid's "ugly" feel comes from a few specific choices. The pale dashed task lines run straight through every event label, so the text looks struck through. The axis is a faint 1.5px gray-lavender line with no arrow and 6px dots, so the timeline spine nearly disappears. Period labels and events use exactly the same type, so the eye can't tell "2004" from "Facebook". And a heavy solid-green section band sits close under the title and outweighs everything else. Fix the connector/text overlap and give the axis and period labels more weight, and flowmaid would clearly beat mermaid here.
flowmaid_better: Correctness: flowmaid draws all 6 periods and 9 events. mermaid 12.2.0 drops 2002 LinkedIn, 2004 Facebook/Google and 2005 YouTube completely, because its renderer only draws tasks whose section matches a declared section (`tasks2.filter((task) => task.section === section)` in timeline-definition-JXYKGLGB.mjs:1124, with no branch for tasks before the first section). That loses information.
Section semantics: flowmaid's 'Mobile' band (x 312-600) covers exactly the 2007/2009/2010 columns, and the unnamed leading group correctly gets no header.
Compactness: 624x201 with even 96px columns and 24px margins. mermaid uses 995x643 for three columns, and its axis runs from x=150 to x=1040, about 250px past the last box (content ends at x=790).
Title is centred over the diagram. mermaid's title is left-anchored at x=145 with font-size 4ex and is not centred over anything.
Contrast: dark #232840 text on white. mermaid puts white text on light lavender (hsl(240,100%,76%) period boxes, even lighter event boxes), which is weak contrast.

No artifacts: mermaid draws pale-yellow 3px `node-line` rules (hsl(60,100%,86%)) under every box and ends each dashed line in an arrowhead that points at empty space below the last event. flowmaid has neither.

Text is vertically centred in the band (dy=0.33em at the band's mid-height). mermaid's 'Mobile', '2007', '2009' and '2010' sit in the upper part of their 66px-tall boxes, leaving a lot of empty space at the bottom of each box.

verified.title: Dashed task lines run through the event labels (strike-through look)
verified.reasoning: I zoomed to 5x (scratchpad/cmp/zv/left.png, right.png) and the strike-through shows on all 9 events: Linke|dIn, Faceb|ook, Goo|gle, YouT|ube, iPh|one, Andr|oid, Whats|App, Insta|gram, Pinte|rest. Each line also leaves a short tail below the last label. The first pass got some letter positions wrong (LinkedIn is split at e|d, not d|I; Facebook at b|o, not e|b), but the substance is right. The geometry explains it. Each line starts at y=127 with dasharray 4,4, so dashes cover 127-131, 135-139, 143-147 and 151-152. LinkedIn's glyphs span about 138-148 (centre 143.5 plus 0.33em), so the 143-147 dash lands mid-glyph. The text is painted after the line, so the dash only shows between and inside letters, which is exactly what makes it read as struck through. The text stays legible because the stroke is a low-contrast 1.2px, but this is the most visible flaw in the render, and it is visible even in the downscaled side-by-side.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:325-331 draws one dashed <line> at x=p.cx from sec.axis_y to p.line_bottom. src/timeline.rs:115-119 sets line_bottom = ey - EVENT_GAP, the bottom of the last event's 17px line box, about 8.5px below its centre. src/timeline.rs:335-337 then draws each event with svg_text_multiline (src/scene.rs:3981), which is bare centred text at the same cx with no background or halo. So the line passes through every event label and runs past the last one.
verified.fix_sketch: Quickest fix (S): give event text a halo so the line breaks around the letters. Add a variant svg_text_multiline_attrs(s,cx,cy,fill,label,extra) in scene.rs and pass extra = stroke="#fff" stroke-width="4" stroke-linejoin="round" paint-order="stroke" for events. Also end the line at the last event's glyph baseline, or at its top, not at line_bottom. Better fix (M): draw each event as a chip, i.e. rect width text_width+16, height lines*LINE_H+4, rx 4, filled with the section colour at about 12% opacity, painted after the line and before the text. The line then shows only in the 8px EVENT_GAPs, as in mermaid, and the chips also fix the grouping and hierarchy issues.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: A pale 1.2px dashed line runs from the axis down through every bare-text event label and sticks out about 4px below the last one.
verified.what_mermaid_does: The dashed line runs behind opaque event boxes, so it only shows in the gaps between boxes.

verified.title: Period labels and events are typographically identical
verified.reasoning: In the SVG, every period and event <text> inherits font-size 13 with normal weight and fill #232840, with no container. In the PNG, '2004' and 'Facebook' look identical. Only their position relative to the faint axis tells 'when' from 'what'. Timeline conventions, and mermaid's darker period boxes over lighter event boxes, give periods more weight.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:334 (period label) and :336 (events) both call svg_text_multiline(&mut s, p.cx, y, TEXT_COLOR, ..). That helper (src/scene.rs:3981-4011) has no font-weight, font-size or class parameter, so the two kinds of text cannot be styled differently.
verified.fix_sketch: Add an attrs-taking variant of svg_text_multiline (it also serves the halo fix above). Emit period labels with font-weight="bold", and optionally fill them with the section colour darkened toward TEXT_COLOR. Alternatively, draw the period as a small filled pill in the section colour, with the text colour picked by contrast. Leave events at regular weight. If periods are bold, adjust period_w (timeline.rs:48) by the 1.06 bold factor.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Periods and events are both 13px, normal weight and #232840, with no container.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Periods are taller, darker boxes and events are lighter boxes.

verified.title: Timeline axis is faint and has no direction arrow
verified.reasoning: The faintness is real. #c2c8dc on white measures 1.67:1, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 guideline for meaningful graphics, and at 1.5px it is lighter than every other element. But 'nearly invisible' is overstated. In both the 1x and the 1.5x PNG the axis reads clearly as a continuous lavender spine with dots on it. The missing arrowhead is a mermaid-parity or stylistic point, not a defect: ascending years left to right already give the direction, and many timeline styles have no arrow.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:37 AXIS_COLOR = "#c2c8dc" is shared by the axis and the dashed task lines. The axis is emitted at src/timeline.rs:309-317 with a hard-coded stroke-width 1.5 and no marker. There is no <defs> or arrow marker in the timeline SVG.
verified.fix_sketch: Split AXIS_COLOR into AXIS_COLOR (darker neutral such as #8a90a8, about 3:1, width 2) and TASK_COLOR (keep #c2c8dc for the dashed lines). For an optional arrow, emit one <marker> after svg_open, put marker-end only on the last section's axis segment, extend that segment by about 10px, and add the same amount to content_w at timeline.rs:183.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: A 1.5px #c2c8dc axis at 1.67:1 contrast, with no arrowhead.
verified.what_mermaid_does: A 4px black axis with an arrowhead marker that runs about 250px past the content.

verified.title: 6px tick dots are the only colour link between columns and their section
verified.reasoning: It is true that only the r=3 dots carry the section colour. 'Nothing visibly belongs to the band' is overstated: the band spans exactly x 312-600, the 2007/2009/2010 columns, and that horizontal extent is a clear, conventional grouping cue in the PNG. A related point the first pass did not make: the unnamed leading group takes accent(0), indigo, so its dots use a colour that no band or legend explains. Its presence also shifts every named section's colour by one.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:39 TICK_R = 3.0. src/timeline.rs:321-324 is the only place sec.color reaches period content. Text (334-336) and task lines (329, AXIS_COLOR) are neutral. src/timeline.rs:172 and :232 call color: accent(si) for every section, including the unnamed implicit one.
verified.fix_sketch: Raise TICK_R to about 4.5 and give it a white 1.5px stroke ring. Tint the task line or event chips with sec.color (see the chip fix in issue 1). Optionally give the unnamed section a neutral grey and index named sections separately so their colours do not shift.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Only the 6px dots are section-coloured. The unnamed group's dots are indigo with nothing to explain the colour.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Every period and event box is filled with its section colour.

verified.title: Dashed line is painted on top of the tick dot
verified.reasoning: At 16x (scratchpad/tlx/dot.png) a pale vertical bar visibly notches the lower half of the indigo dot. In the SVG the <circle> comes before the <line>, and the line starts at the dot's centre. At 1x it is a 1.2px stripe on a 6px dot, barely noticeable, so it is cosmetic.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:321-324 emits the circle, then src/timeline.rs:325-331 emits the dashed line from y1 = sec.axis_y, the dot's centre, so the line is painted over the dot.
verified.fix_sketch: Swap the two push_str blocks so the circle comes after the line, or start the line at sec.axis_y + TICK_R. A two-line change.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The pale dash crosses the lower half of each coloured dot.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Has no dots. The dashed line starts below the period box.

verified.title: Solid green section band dominates and leaves the composition lopsided
verified.reasoning: Mostly subjective. The band is the heaviest mass, but mermaid's band is equally heavy and bigger. The empty top-left above 2002-2005 is the correct outcome: the implicit leading group has no name, so it gets no header, and the first pass itself praised this under 'section semantics'. The measurable problem here is contrast. White bold 13px 'Mobile' on #33a35c is 3.21:1, which fails the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for non-large text. That item is listed under missed defects.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:294-305 draws a solid rect in sec.color with hard-coded white bold text. src/timeline.rs:156-161 reserves band_h = SECTION_H across the full width whenever any section is named, which is intended.
verified.fix_sketch: Use a lighter band: section colour at about 15-18% fill-opacity with a 3px solid top or left accent bar, and the text in the section colour darkened to at least 4.5:1. Alternatively keep the solid band and pick the text colour by luminance (see missed defects).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: A solid #33a35c 288x30 band with white bold text over the right half. The top-left band row is empty.
verified.what_mermaid_does: A solid lavender band over all of its (fewer) columns, with equally heavy boxes beneath.

verified.title: Title sits too close to the section band
verified.reasoning: Measured from the 4x crop (scratchpad/tlx/title.png): title baseline about 46.6, descender bottom about 50, band top 58, so about 8-11px of clearance. That is less than the band-to-period-label gap (about 16px), and there is about 34px of space above the title's cap height (24px PAD plus half of TITLE_H). So the title sits nearer the content than the canvas edge, but cramped against the band. It is a minor spacing imbalance.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:195 title_pos = (width/2, PAD + TITLE_H/2) centres the title in a 34px band. Lines 143-146 then start content at top = PAD + TITLE_H with no extra title-to-content gap. layout_td repeats this at lines 210-213 and 255.
verified.fix_sketch: Add const TITLE_GAP: f64 = 10.0 and use top += TITLE_H + TITLE_GAP (and the same for y in layout_td), or move title_pos up by about 4px (PAD + TITLE_H/2 - 4).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: About 8-11px between the 17px title and the band top, against about 34px above the title.
verified.what_mermaid_does: About 30px between the title baseline (y=20) and the band (y=50).

verified.title: Flat, small type scale (13px everywhere, 17px title)
verified.reasoning: The values are accurate: root font-size 13 and title 17. But 13px is a flowmaid house constant shared by architecture.rs:29, gitgraph.rs:29, journey.rs:37 and sankey.rs:22, so this is a project-wide style choice, not a timeline defect. The 17/13 title ratio is a real level of hierarchy. The 'flat' part duplicates no-period-event-hierarchy. At native size the text is small but legible.
verified.root_cause: src/timeline.rs:35 FONT: u32 = 13 is passed to svg_open (line 275). The title size of 17 is hard-coded at line 281. Note that text_width is calibrated at 14px (src/layout.rs:173), so the 13px text is slightly over-measured.
verified.fix_sketch: If a change is wanted, set the timeline FONT to 14, which matches the text_width calibration, and fix the hierarchy with bold periods rather than more sizes. Decide this across all 13px diagram types for consistency.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: 13px body text and a 17px bold title.
verified.what_mermaid_does: 16px body text and a 4ex bold title.

missed: White section-band text fails contrast, and this input triggers it. 'Mobile' is bold 13px #fff on #33a35c at 3.21:1, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for text under 18.66px bold. 6 of the 8 ACCENTS fail with white: green 3.21, amber #d99114 2.62, teal 3.47, coral 3.55, steel 3.50, rose 4.14. A third section (amber) gives 2.62:1, see scratchpad/tlx/td.svg 'Social'. Root cause: src/timeline.rs:301 hard-codes fill="#ffffff" whatever sec.color is. Fix (S): pick the text colour per band by relative luminance (white if contrast with sec.color is at least 4.5, else TEXT_COLOR), or switch to the lighter band style. This also counters the first pass's 'flowmaid has better contrast' claim.

Section names wider than their columns overflow the band and turn invisible. Not triggered by this input, but trivially reachable. With `section Mobile and smartphone revolution era` over a single period, the band is 96px wide and the bold white name (about 240px) is centred at x=72, so the text spills off the left canvas edge (clipped) and across the neighbouring 'Web' band. Outside a band it is white on white and disappears. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/tlx/longsec.png, which shows only 'smartphone rev'. Root cause: src/timeline.rs:166-167 (LR) and :226-227 (TD) set the band width to the sum of period_w (lines 47-53, which measure only period and event text), never compared with text_width(&sec.name)*1.06 + 2*COL_PAD. to_svg_with (lines 299-305) neither clips nor truncates. Fix (S-M): compute name_w and, when it exceeds the columns' width, spread the extra evenly across that section's columns (pass a min total width into layout_section_periods). Severity 3 when triggered.

Long titles are clipped at both canvas edges, and content stays left-aligned when the title widens the canvas. Not triggered by this input. `title A very long title for a tiny timeline that is much wider` gives a 374px canvas, but the 17px bold title is about 420px, so 'A v' and 'der' are cut off (scratchpad/tlx/longtitle.png). The single column also hugs the left edge under the centred title. Root cause: src/timeline.rs:193 and :253 compute title_w = text_width(t) + 2*PAD, where text_width is calibrated for 14px regular (src/layout.rs:173), but line 281 renders at 17px bold, about 1.29x wider. Sections always start at x=PAD (lines 164 and 233) and are never re-centred when width > content_w. journey.rs:134 has the same width bug. Fix (S): title_w = text_width(t) * 17.0/TEXT_CALIBRATION * 1.06 + 2*PAD, and offset every section's x by (width - content_w)/2.

Long events and periods are never wrapped. One long event (`2007 : The first iPhone was announced by Steve Jobs at Macworld in San Francisco`) gives a 657px-wide single column, while mermaid wraps event text at its box width (wrap() in timeline-definition-JXYKGLGB.mjs:946). Root cause: src/timeline.rs:47-53 period_w uses the unwrapped text_width, and line_count only counts explicit
breaks. Fix (M): word-wrap events and periods to a max column width (about 160-180px) before layout, store the result as '\n'-joined text so line_count and svg_text_multiline handle it unchanged.

name: sankey
diagram_type: sankey
overall_verdict: For this sankey, flowmaid does not look ugly. It is about as good as mermaid and better in several places. Canvas, column positions, node width and gradient links are the same, and flowmaid has fewer ribbon crossings, better-centred labels drawn on top of the ribbons, and a real margin. The visible weaknesses are in colour and label placement. An 8-colour palette that wraps around gives three node-colour clashes (Losses is the same green as Electricity, Homes the same blue as Coal, Industry light the same orange as Gas). The Electricity and Industry labels land on nearly the same line, so they read as one run of text. Labels are 13px where mermaid uses 14px, and the one crossing left could be removed.
flowmaid_better: Fewer crossings: flowmaid's barycentre ordering puts Heating above Electricity and 'Industry, light' at the top of the right column, which leaves exactly 1 crossing (Coal->Electricity x Gas->Heating). Mermaid has 4: Gas->Heating crosses Nuclear, Wind and Solar->Electricity, and Heating->Homes crosses Electricity->Losses. Each crossing makes a muddy patch in mermaid's output.

Labels are centred on their nodes: flowmaid uses dy="0.33em" at the node's mid-y. Mermaid uses dy="0em", so the baseline sits on the node centre and every label rides about 5px high. For example, 'Coal 42 TWh' sits at PNG y~70 while the Coal node centre is y~77.

Labels draw above the ribbons: flowmaid emits them after the paths. Mermaid emits <g class="node-labels"> before <g class="links">, so 0.5-opacity multiply-blended ribbons are painted over the text and tint it.
Clearer value formatting: flowmaid prints 'Coal (42 TWh)'. Mermaid's 'Coal\n42 TWh' collapses to 'Coal 42 TWh', so name and number run together, e.g. 'Industry, light 6 TWh'.
Breathing room: flowmaid has a 24px margin (PAD). Mermaid's nodes touch the SVG edges: Coal at y=0, Solar ending at y=400, left nodes at x=0, right nodes at x=590-600.
Thicker ribbons despite the margin: 2.14 px/TWh in flowmaid (Coal 89.9px for 42) against 2.06 px/TWh in mermaid (86.4px).
Hover tooltips: every ribbon has a <title> (e.g. 'Coal → Electricity: 42 TWh'), every node has one too, plus role=img and aria-label. Mermaid's sankey has none.
Smaller, self-contained SVG: 6.9 KB against 10.4 KB, with no large unrelated CSS block.

verified.title: 8-colour accent cycle gives 3 node-colour clashes; Losses looks like part of Electricity
verified.reasoning: Checked against the SVG. Node indices in first-appearance order are Coal 0, Electricity 1, Gas 2, Heating 3, Nuclear 4, Wind 5, Solar 6, Industry 7, Homes 8, Losses 9, Industry light 10. With accent(i % 8): Homes and Coal are both #5b6dc0, Losses and Electricity are both #33a35c, Industry light and Gas are both #d99114. Gradient fmsk-...-8 (Electricity->Losses) has #33a35c at both stops, so in the PNG that ribbon is flat green and the Losses bar reads as a continuation of the hub. Mermaid uses scaleOrdinal(schemeTableau10) keyed by node id (sankeyDiagram-SY24JHO5.mjs:688), so it has one clash (Industry light = Coal #4e79a7), on nodes far apart. One correction to the first pass: the Homes=Coal clash does little harm because the two are at opposite edges. The more visible damage comes from near-identical hues placed next to each other. Homes (#5b6dc0 indigo) sits directly above Industry (#4d8fbf steel blue) in the right column, so the two largest outgoing ribbons are both green-to-blue and hard to tell apart. Nuclear teal (#199a8e) next to Electricity green makes Nuclear->Electricity almost one colour.
verified.root_cause: src/sankey.rs:446 `color: accent(i)` colours each node by its declaration index only, ignoring links and column neighbours. src/style.rs:84-98: ACCENTS has only 8 entries and accent() wraps with `index % ACCENTS.len()`. The palette also holds two near-duplicate pairs, indigo #5b6dc0 / steel blue #4d8fbf (idx 0 and 7) and green #33a35c / teal #199a8e (idx 1 and 4). src/sankey.rs:543 takes the gradient stops straight from the endpoint node colours, so a same-colour pair gives a flat ribbon.
verified.fix_sketch: Give sankey its own colour assignment (leave style::accent alone because ER etc. depend on it). (1) Use a palette of at least 10-12 clearly distinct hues, e.g. a Tableau10-like list plus 2. (2) After `cols` has been ordered (~line 404), colour nodes greedily in index order: start from palette[i % len] and skip any colour already used by a link neighbour (source or target) or by the node directly above or below in the same column. Optionally treat indigo/steel and green/teal as conflicting. Deterministic and about 30 lines. (3) Optional: honour mermaid 12's `sankey.nodeColors` map (mermaid uses it in getNodeColor). flowmaid's parser ignores it today (no match for nodeColors in src). Add a test that no link has identical source and target colours and no two vertically adjacent nodes share a colour.
verified.what_mermaid_does: d3 schemeTableau10 via scaleOrdinal on node id: 10 hues for 11 nodes, one distant clash (Industry light = Coal).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: ACCENTS[i % 8]: Homes=Coal, Losses=Electricity (flat green ribbon), Industry light=Gas. Homes (indigo) and Industry (steel blue) are stacked next to each other in near-identical blues.

verified.title: 'Electricity (124 TWh)' and 'Industry (48 TWh)' sit on nearly the same line; no label collision handling at all
verified.reasoning: The SVG has Electricity text at x=311, y=225.3 (start) and Industry at x=560, y=229.5 (end), only 4.2px apart vertically. Measured in the 1.5x PNG with the 10px frame removed, Electricity spans x 312-433 and Industry spans x 457-561, a gap of about 24px. At the default size they do NOT overlap; they just read as one line of two items. 'Read as one phrase' is somewhat overstated. The latent risk the first pass claimed is real, though. I re-rendered the same source with `width: 450` and 'Electricity (124 TWh)' prints directly over 'Industry (48 TWh)' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/sk/narrow.png). Renaming Industry to 'Heavy industry and manufacturing' at the default 600px gives a full overprint (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/sk/long.png). The near-alignment is systematic, not chance: every column is centred on the plot's mid-height, so the big central node of the middle column and the central node of the right column both land near y=200. It also persists after the crossing fix (bwd.png).
verified.root_cause: src/sankey.rs:433-451: label_pos = (x +/- LABEL_GAP, node centre). The side depends only on the column index (last column gets 'end', every other column gets 'start'), and nothing checks label against label. sankey.rs never measures text: it does not import layout::text_width, unlike pie.rs and journey.rs. The comment at 433-434 ('so they never sit on top of a ribbon') is wrong for both middle and edge columns. Contributing: src/sankey.rs:417-428 centres each column on its own in the plot area, which lines up the middle-height nodes of adjacent columns.
verified.fix_sketch: After nodes are placed (~line 452), add a label pass. Estimate each label box as width = layout::text_width(text) * FONT/13 and height of about 1.2*FONT, anchored per label_anchor. For every start-anchored label in a non-last column, test it against the labels of column c+1 (both anchors) with about 8px clearance. On a conflict, try other y positions inside the node's span (centre +/- k*1.3*FONT, clamped to [y+0.6em, y+h-0.6em]), then try the left side (end anchor at x-LABEL_GAP, checked against column c-1). Take the first position with no conflict and fall back to the centre. Optionally add mermaid 12's `labelStyle: outlined` white halo (paint-order: stroke) so text over ribbons and other text stays readable. Regression test: the corpus with width 450 must yield no overlapping label boxes.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Also has no collision handling (labels go right if x0 < width/2, else left). Here its ordering happens to separate Electricity (y=127.5) from Industry (y=49) and Homes (y=179).
verified.what_flowmaid_does: The middle-column label sits at the Electricity centre (y=225.3). The right-column Industry label is at y=229.5 with about 24px between them. There is no measurement or collision check, so width 450 or a longer sink name gives a direct overprint.

verified.title: Remaining Coal->Electricity x Gas->Heating crossing is avoidable: forward-only barycentre never reorders column 0; passes 2-4 are no-ops
verified.reasoning: Counted crossings in both renders. flowmaid has exactly 1 (Coal->Electricity 24-113.9 => 92.5-182.5 against Gas->Heating 125.9-164.5 => 42-80.5). Mermaid has 4 (Gas->Heating crosses Nuclear, Wind and Solar->Electricity, and Heating->Homes crosses Electricity->Losses). The code does what the claim says: only columns 1..n are sorted, each keyed on column c-1, so column 0 keeps declaration order. Because column c depends only on column c-1, and the tie-break is the current rank, which is already sorted after pass 1, passes 2-4 change nothing. To test, I copied the repo to the scratchpad and added a backward sweep (columns n-2..0 keyed on the targets' ranks in column c+1). Gas (barycentre 0.5) moves above Coal (1.0) and the render has ZERO crossings (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/sk/bwd.png). All 43 sankey unit tests still pass. Severity 1 is fair because flowmaid already beats mermaid here, but this crossing is the biggest muddy patch in the flowmaid render.
verified.root_cause: src/sankey.rs:366-399: `for _ in 0..ORDER_PASSES { for c in 1..n_cols { let prev = cols[c-1] ...` has no reverse sweep, so cols[0] is never permuted and later passes recompute identical orders. The doc comment at 25-28 ('four sweeps is where the layout stops visibly improving') is false. Secondary: the barycentre uses unweighted rank position, not value-weighted y.
verified.fix_sketch: Inside the ORDER_PASSES loop, after the forward sweep, add a backward sweep `for c in (0..n_cols-1).rev()` keyed on the mean rank in cols[c+1] of each node's targets (the same sort and tie-break as the forward sweep). Prototype is about 25 lines and gives 0 crossings here with tests green. To be robust, count ribbon crossings after each sweep (pairs of links between the same column pair whose source and target ranks invert) and keep the best ordering, since alternating sweeps can oscillate. Optionally weight barycentres by link value.
verified.what_mermaid_does: d3-sankey relaxation leaves 4 crossings for this input.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Column 0 keeps declaration order (Coal, Gas, Nuclear, Wind, Solar), which leaves 1 crossing where the 90px Coal ribbon passes under the 38px Gas->Heating ribbon.

verified.title: Node labels are 13px against mermaid's 14px
verified.reasoning: The flowmaid root <svg> has font-size="13" and every label inherits it. Mermaid's <g class="node-labels" font-size="14"> is hard-coded in sankeyDiagram-SY24JHO5.mjs:717, and its fill #333 comes from the root CSS. The difference is real but cosmetic. Visually flowmaid's labels are only slightly smaller, and its TEXT_COLOR #232840 is darker than #333, so they don't read as much lighter. Severity 1.
verified.root_cause: src/sankey.rs:22 `pub const FONT: u32 = 13;`, passed to svg_open at src/sankey.rs:530.
verified.fix_sketch: Set FONT = 14. Check the knock-on effect: with node_padding 12 (model.rs:1373) and labels centred on nodes, two adjacent tiny nodes would have label centres about 13px apart, which is tighter than a 14px line. Either raise the effective padding when show_values is on (mermaid adds 15 to nodePadding when showValues is true) or let the label pass from the collision fix enforce a minimum spacing.
verified.what_mermaid_does: node-labels group at font-size 14, fill #333.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: font-size 13 on the root, fill #232840.

missed: Adjacent same-hue nodes (more visible than the clashes the first pass listed): Homes rect fill #5b6dc0 sits directly above Industry rect fill #4d8fbf in the right column, so the Electricity->Homes (40) and Electricity->Industry (48) ribbons are both green-to-blue gradients and nearly indistinguishable in sankey.flowmaid.png. Nuclear #199a8e next to Electricity #33a35c gives an almost flat ribbon. Root cause: src/style.rs:84-93 ACCENTS holds two blues (idx 0, 7) and green/teal (idx 1, 4), and src/sankey.rs:446 never considers adjacency. Same fix as palette-wrap-collisions.

No text measurement anywhere in src/sankey.rs (unlike pie.rs and journey.rs, which use layout::text_width), so label collisions become actual overprints with ordinary inputs. Same source with `width: 450`: 'Electricity (124 TWh)' prints over 'Industry (48 TWh)' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/sk/narrow.png). A longer sink name at the default 600px gives a full overprint (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-flowmaid/cac93b13-7009-5470-94b5-477c61df0333/scratchpad/sk/long.png). This makes collinear-mid-right-labels a severity-2 latent defect, not a cosmetic one.

Latent, not in this diagram: a link that skips a column, which justify alignment can produce, is drawn as a straight band through intermediate-column nodes and their ribbons. Test 'A,C,10 / A,B,10 / B,D,30 / B,C,5 / E,B,25': A->C (y 24-99.6) runs across node B's rect (x 295, y 67.8-332.2). Also, link stacking at src/sankey.rs:459-462 compares order[] ranks across different columns and breaks ties by declaration order. d3-sankey shares the pass-through weakness, so low priority.

Misleading code comments that hide the two layout defects: src/sankey.rs:25-28 says four ordering sweeps improve the layout (passes 2-4 are no-ops), and src/sankey.rs:433-434 says labels 'never sit on top of a ribbon' (every label in this render sits on a ribbon). Not visual, but they explain why these defects went unnoticed.

name: architecture
diagram_type: architecture-beta
overall_verdict: Mermaid 12.2.0's own render of this diagram is broken in places. Web App and Mobile App sit on the same spot, so their labels merge into "MWobile App". Four of the six services show a "?" icon. The svc-cache line also runs through the "Business Logic" label. At a glance flowmaid looks tidier, but it reads as a long, short strip of plain boxes with tiny emoji, not as an architecture diagram. Worse, 2 of the 5 edges are drawn wrong: the web edge is hidden behind Mobile App, so the boxes look chained, and the svc-cache edge runs along node borders and through the PostgreSQL box, so Redis looks unconnected. The cause is the layout. It lays groups out in one row and services in a grid in source order, ignoring edges and port sides. The router then draws a simple Z-shaped line with no obstacle avoidance and no idea which way a port faces.
flowmaid_better: No overlapping nodes: mermaid puts web and mobile at the same translate(-305.8,-155.8), so the labels merge into 'MWobile App' and both edges share one path. Flowmaid gives each service its own box.
Every service gets an icon. Mermaid's built-in icon set has no web, mobile, cpu or cache, so it draws a big '?' tile for Web App, Mobile App, Business Logic and Redis.
Edges between R and L ports are straight and horizontal at the node centre line (y=109). Mermaid draws the svc:R<->L:db edge as a long diagonal from the corner of the Business Logic tile.

(2) Generate candidate paths between the stubs: two L-shapes, plus Z-shapes whose middle channel is either the midpoint or the centre of a free gap taken from the sorted node and group x/y extents. (3) Keep the shortest candidate whose segments miss every service rect inflated by about 6px. Here that gives 727,144 727,160 1064,160 1064,58 1153,58 1153,74, which runs under the boxes, up the gap between PostgreSQL and Redis, and into the top of Redis. This fixes the current output without any layout change; the port-aware layout (see layout-ignores-ports-and-edges) removes the detour altogether.

verified.title: The layout ignores edges and port directions (B/T placement, fan-in): one row in source order
verified.reasoning: In the code, edges are read only after every position is fixed (line 203 onward). All six services are at y=74. A source-order experiment confirms it: swapping the db and cache declarations swaps their x positions, after which the svc<->db edge (802,109 to 1078,109) passes straight through Redis. Placement depends only on declaration order. Mermaid builds spatial maps from the port pairs and feeds fcose relativePlacementConstraint and alignmentConstraint (mermaid.core architectureDiagram-ZHVYKT53.mjs:1034 getRelativeConstraints, :1182-1183).
verified.root_cause: src/architecture.rs:124-142: top-level groups are placed left to right at y=PAD (x += w + GROUP_GAP). Lines 251-342: layout_group puts children in a ceil(sqrt(n))-column grid in source order. Lines 376-386: port() is the only code that consults ArchSide, and it runs after placement.
verified.fix_sketch: Port a simple version of mermaid's spatial map. (1) For each connected component, BFS from the first service and give each service integer cell coordinates: (R,L) adds 1 column, (L,R) subtracts 1, (B,T) adds 1 row, (T,B) subtracts 1, mixed pairs move diagonally. (2) Resolve cell collisions by pushing perpendicular to the edge direction, which stacks web and mobile vertically. (3) Keep groups contiguous: sort each group's member cells, compute group rectangles, and when two group rectangles overlap, shift the later group and everything beyond it along the axis of least overlap. (4) Convert cells to pixels with per-column widths and per-row heights plus GROUP_PAD/GAP. (5) Fall back to the current grid for services with no edges. Nested groups and conflicting constraints (svc->db says Data is to the right, svc->cache says Data is below) need tie-breaking; mermaid's staircase is one acceptable answer. Add regression tests asserting that cache.x≈svc.x, cache.y>svc.y, and that web and mobile share a column.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: Groups go in one row and services in a sqrt grid in source order. Ports never affect placement.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Port directions drive placement: R->L puts the target to the right, B->T puts it below. The result is a Frontend/Backend/Data staircase with cache directly under svc.

verified.title: The orthogonal router ignores which way a port faces and has no obstacle avoidance
verified.reasoning: orthogonal_route(a, b) has no access to port sides at all. Every edge here is either straight (dy==0) or a horizontal-first Z. The B-port edge leaves sideways along svc's own bottom border, and the T-port edge arrives sideways along Redis's top border. An ungrouped test case, a:R -- L:b with b at the origin, produced 198,109 99,109 99,35 0,35. That edge leaves a's R port and doubles back left across a's own box, which shows that facing is ignored even in trivial cases. No code checks for collisions, and drawing edges under nodes hides every overlap.
verified.root_cause: src/architecture.rs:206 calls orthogonal_route(p0, p1) and drops e.from_side and e.to_side. Lines 388-401 choose the bend orientation only from |dx| vs |dy| and return a straight segment if either is ~0. Lines 452-511 draw edges before nodes.
verified.fix_sketch: Change the signature to orthogonal_route(a, sa, b, sb, rects). Always emit an outward stub (side_normal * 14). Pick the bend orientation so the first and last segments run along the port normals: for a vertical-out to vertical-in pair use a Z with a horizontal middle, for horizontal pairs a Z with a vertical middle, and for mixed pairs an L. If the target lies behind the port, use a U around the node. Score candidates by length plus a large penalty for each node rect crossed, and pick the lowest. router.rs has stub_of and side_move helpers (lines 2620-2645), but they are tied to the flowchart Ctx/Graph, so a self-contained version of about 150 lines in architecture.rs is simpler.
verified.what_flowmaid_does: It produces a horizontal-first Z or a straight line whatever the port side, with no collision checks.
verified.what_mermaid_does: Edges leave and enter along their port normals. The B-T edge here is a single vertical segment.

verified.title: Icons are 16px emoji: too small to give the 'architecture' look, and mixed colour and monochrome
verified.reasoning: In the PNG, 🖥, 🗄 and the ☁/🖥/🗄 group-title glyphs render black and monochrome, while 🌐📱🧠⚡ render in colour. I found the precise cause: U+2601, U+1F5A5 and U+1F5C4 have Emoji_Presentation=No, so without a U+FE0F variation selector Chrome draws them with the text font. When I re-rendered a copy of the SVG with U+FE0F appended to those three, every glyph came out in colour (scratchpad rv_arch/vs16.png). U+2709 ✉ in icon_glyph has the same problem. The 16px size and the platform-dependent font fallback are as the first pass described.
verified.root_cause: src/architecture.rs:38-65: icon_glyph returns bare text-presentation code points for cloud ("☁"), database ("🗄"), server and code ("🖥"), and mail ("✉"), with no \u{FE0F}. ICON_FONT=16 (line 31). The group title prefixes the glyph inline at FONT=13 (lines 156-158, 446).

Better fix (M): ship a small table of built-in vector icon paths (cloud, database cylinder, server rack, disk, internet) drawn as inline <path> at 28-36px, either as a coloured tile like mermaid's or inline in the card. This stays zero-dependency and renders the same in rsvg, resvg and browsers. Keep emoji as the fallback for other names.

verified.what_mermaid_does: It shows 80x80 vector icon tiles (white on #087ebf), consistent everywhere, with '?' for unknown names.
